scopeNotes: Footprints of the three imported records were inspected and cover substantially the same island group. Modern independence is dated separately from the 1715, 1815 and 1914 record starts. Exact geometry remains unverified.
The narrative does not assign all Grenadines to this state; Grenada, Carriacou and Petite Martinique have their own geographic narrative.

Argyle house functions are interpretations from plans and historical comparison. A reconstructed village is not a surviving sixteenth-century building. The source’s exclusive first-and-only claims are omitted.

The West India Committee publication was downloaded and read in selected passages. Its poorly supported early ethnic replacement narrative, shipwreck origin certainty, alleged cannibalism, unique-art claims and timeline errors are excluded. The ladle remains an attributed object with uncertain provenance; motifs do not establish genetic or geographic ancestry.

Chatoyer’s death is dated to the war in 1795, without adopting inconsistent day-level accounts or a purported duel. The 1779 capture follows the main text, not its erroneous 1776 timeline. Captivity and mortality on Balliceaux precede the 1797 exile; exact population and casualty totals are not asserted.
The Garifuna Heritage Foundation annual report supports exile and enduring connections. Its old population estimates and future program proposals are not converted to present facts.

Boa’s research abstract was read; the full article was inaccessible. The card uses its stated findings only. A British Online Archives introduction incorrectly denying apprenticeship on Saint Vincent was rejected; the article and contemporary 1838 records establish the distinction.

The UNIDO brief is dated December 2019 despite later search crawl metadata. It documents existing machinery and plans, not a completed factory. Production statistics, forecast capacities and obsolete trade prices are omitted.

The legislative overview’s broad claim to the first organized government and conflation of 1838 with abolition are not adopted. The original constitution order confirms independence on 27 October 1979.

UNESCO’s Garifuna element has ID 00001. Indexed English content appeared under an erroneous carnival slug; the canonical Garifuna URL and matching French record identify the correct element. Contemporary schooling statistics in the old description are not repeated.

The 2022 eruption paper was read in selected monitoring and crisis-response sections. These are historical events, not current hazard advice. Forecasts remain probabilistic; evacuation totals varying by geographic scope are omitted.
No successor links are invented from one geographic snapshot to another. Independent historical, depth and geometry reviews remain pending.
